inspection_summary: Inspected all 3,393 normalized lines of the 1992 article. The source develops a direct-counting nonvanishing method for Dirichlet L-functions: Barban-Vehov cancellation weights define a mollifier, a contour shift and functional equation split a smoothed detector into L(s,chi)M(s,chi)+I+J, mean and mean-square estimates separate zero from nonzero characters, and a long diagonal analysis yields the I-term main constant before fixed-point and interval results. Prose, theorem boundaries, and strategic dependencies are coherent; many display formulas are OCR-degraded, so exact coefficients, exponents, and constants in formula-dependent units require scan verification.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic identity, title, and section map; no substantive mathematical unit.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Frames central-line nonvanishing, explains the limitation of raw moment inequalities, states the two main results, and previews the direct-counting mollifier strategy.

sections_inspected.label: 1. The Barban-Vehov weights
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines cancellation weights and derives mean-square, progression, and shifted-convolution controls used by the mollifier estimates.

sections_inspected.label: 2. The mollifier polynomial
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Chooses the two cutoff scales, builds the mollifier, records its coefficient gap, and bounds its character mean square.

sections_inspected.label: 3. The basic equation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses Mellin inversion, contour shifting, the functional equation, and Dirichlet-series truncation to obtain S=LM+I+J and control the tail J.

sections_inspected.label: 4. The mean and mean square of S
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Computes the detector's first moment and second moment by character orthogonality, shifted-convolution control, and diagonal evaluation.

sections_inspected.label: 5. The integral R_a(s,y)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces the kernel governing I and gives residue expansions with controlled contour remainders in the two y regimes.

sections_inspected.label: 6. An expression for the mean square of I
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Applies parity-sensitive character orthogonality to convert the I mean square into coupled arithmetic sums and identifies the intended diagonal.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Estimate of the non-diagonal terms
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Shows the negative-congruence contribution and principal-character correction are negligible.

sections_inspected.label: 8. The diagonal terms
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Expands the kernel on the diagonal, bounds the residue tail, and reduces the I mean square to a structured main arithmetic sum.

sections_inspected.label: 9. Analysis of the main term
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Parametrizes diagonal quadruples by gcd data, expands the weights, proves a support/error lemma, and obtains a tractable expression for N(sigma).

sections_inspected.label: 10. The main term: continued
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Evaluates the arithmetic main term through Euler products and partial summation, producing the mean-square asymptotic and error regimes.

sections_inspected.label: 11. Non-vanishing at a fixed point
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines the basic equation, first moment, and second moments with Cauchy-Schwarz to lower-bound the number of nonvanishing characters at a fixed point.

sections_inspected.label: 12. Non-vanishing at a variable point
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Covers a real segment by short intervals and circles, converts a zero into a controlled tail expression, and sums exponentially decaying bad-character bounds.

sections_inspected.label: References and author addresses
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography and publication metadata; no new mathematical mechanism.
